inputMessages.content: Hello Samir! I'd love to get to know you a little before your stay at Le Pavillon de la Reine, so the team can think about the details that matter to you. This chat is optional; you can skip a question or finish whenever you like. What brings you here this time?
I'm travelling alone for work, with meetings most of the day. I'd like the evenings to feel a bit less like work.
After a day of meetings, what would help you switch off and make the evening feel like your own?
A good dinner somewhere I can sit at the counter, maybe some live blues one evening.
A counter dinner and some live blues sound like a good change of pace. What kind of food would you most enjoy, and is there anything you avoid?
Grilled fish would be great. I avoid heavy cream sauces, but I don't have allergies.
Is there a blues artist or style you particularly enjoy, or is it more about finding a welcoming spot with good live music?
Buddy Guy is a favourite. A friendly place matters more than a big-name act.

A friendly room with good blues, rather than a headline name—that helps. On meeting mornings, what makes for a good start: do you like to take time over breakfast, or keep it quick with coffee and something small?
A quick breakfast and double espresso after an easy run. Half an hour running usually sets me up well.
An easy half-hour run before breakfast sounds like a good way to start a meeting day. Would you appreciate a suggested running route from the hotel, or do you prefer to find your own way?
A simple route would help. I need to leave the hotel at 8:15, so nothing too ambitious.
A simple half-hour route would fit that early start. Around what time do your meetings usually finish, so dinner and music suggestions fit your evenings?
Meetings are nine until half six, and I usually eat around eight.

result.reply: Dinner around eight leaves a little breathing room after your meetings. Is there anything that makes a particular difference to a good night’s sleep when you’re travelling?
